s682.content:
Theodore was born at an inn in the village of Sykeon in Galatia, in Asia Minor. As a boy he spent long hours in prayer in a nearby chapel, and he grew into a severe ascetic who lived for a time in a cave and in an iron cage.

He was ordained, founded monasteries, and against his will became bishop of Anastasiopolis, though he later resigned to return to the monastic life. Crowds came to him for healing and help, and a disciple named George wrote a long, lively Life of him.
s682.intercession: St. Theodore, pray for us. Bring healing to the sick, and peace to all who are troubled. Amen.

s683.content:
Lucian was a priest and teacher in Antioch, known for his careful scholarship on the text of the Greek Bible. His revision of the Greek Old Testament and the New Testament was widely used in the churches of Syria and Asia Minor.

During the persecution under Maximinus he was arrested and taken to Nicomedia, where he died for the faith in 312. Eusebius records that he made a speech in defense of the faith before the judge.
s683.intercession: St. Lucian, pray for us. Bless all who study and translate the Scriptures. Amen.

s684.content:
Dionysius was a member of the Areopagus, the high council of Athens, who believed when he heard St. Paul preach there about the unknown god, as the Acts of the Apostles records (Acts 17:34). An early tradition says he became the first bishop of Athens and died a martyr.

Around the year 500 a Syrian writer published deep works of mystical theology under his name, and these writings, by the author called Pseudo-Dionysius, influenced theologians of both East and West for a thousand years.
s684.intercession: St. Dionysius, pray for us. Open our minds to the God who is beyond all knowing, and our hearts to his word. Amen.

s685.content:
Pantaenus was a Stoic philosopher who became a Christian and led the catechetical school of Alexandria, the first great Christian school of theology. His most famous student was Clement of Alexandria, who called him a “Sicilian bee” that gathered the honey of the apostles and prophets.

Eusebius records that Pantaenus also went as a missionary to the East, as far as “India,” where he was said to have found Christians who already had the Gospel of Matthew in Hebrew letters.
s685.intercession: St. Pantaenus, pray for us. Bless all who teach the faith, and give us wisdom joined to love. Amen.

s686.content:
In February 2015, twenty Coptic Christian laborers from Egypt and a companion from Ghana, who had gone to Libya to work and support their families, were beheaded on a beach near Sirte by Islamic State militants. A video of their deaths showed many of them praying the name of Jesus.

The Coptic Orthodox Church soon proclaimed them saints. In 2023 Pope Francis, with Pope Tawadros II, announced that they would be included in the Roman Martyrology, a sign of the “ecumenism of blood” that unites Christians who die for Christ.
s686.intercession: Holy Coptic Martyrs, pray for us. Strengthen persecuted Christians everywhere, and bring all Christians to unity. Amen.
